ratings_why.fun: Placing Lurkers beside fodder and watching a death pop a row of Lids is a great fight moment, and the wait-or-strike pull gives real drafting choices; the Patient build is quieter to watch.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: the opponent's preview shows closed Lids, so the board you show is not the board you fight with, and the knock is tied to slot neighbours; no tribe today or generic auto-battler does that.

verdict_why: The core reads well, but three cards (Worshipful Master, Inner Guard, Wafer-Lid Sentry) need wording a player can follow without asking.

points.text: The Worshipful Master's "every Spring effect your units had this fight happens again" is hard to read: say whether it repeats only Spring triggers or also Spring attacks, and where repeated summons go.
Inner Guard's Start of Combat and Lurk's own Start of Combat both fire at once; say that Lurkers go under their Lids first, so the Guard has something to Spring.
Wafer-Lid Sentry doesn't say which Lurker Springs when the attacked unit has two Lurkers next to it; "the first in reading order" would settle it.
The Lurk keyword is long for a card; the card could carry "Lurk" plus a short reminder ("hidden until a neighbour dies") and leave the rest to the glossary.
Ballot Clerk could tie to the ballot box fantasy, for example paying gold when a Lurker stays shut, so the Lodge's one economy card feels like the Lodge.

standouts.why: Signora Corkhinge's lid that closes again is the lore, the mechanic and a clear fight moment all in one line.
Heath Wolf Mother reads at a glance: she pops up, drops her young, and the young are new knocks.
Tapwell, waiting outside and growing while nobody lets him in, is a one-line card that teaches Patient.

weakest.why: Grit-Dresser is a generic end-of-turn buff with only a name to tie it to the Lodge.
Lodge Initiate is a plain enabler with a vanilla body; the initiation fantasy isn't in what it does.
Ballot Clerk's gold is thin and tied to Patience, which stalls on losing streaks.

flags.note: What "happens again" covers, and where repeated summons land, isn't clear.
Order against Lurk's own Start of Combat step is not stated.
No rule for which of two neighbouring Lurkers Springs.
With an all-Lurker board, every Lurker Springs at Start of Combat with double-damage Cleave hits.
Mabyn makes every Lurker Patient and gives +3/+3 each turn on top of the other Patient buffers.
